message.reasoning_content:
Let me work out the phase. I'm in the "check" phase. I must invoke exactly one handoff tool: `diagnosis.check_request`. The other tools available are reads, but the phase says "After at most two successful reading turns, then select the check." Actually the instruction: "Invoke a native tool with its business fields directly... Use exactly one call, or up to three independent evidence reads."

Let me decide the check. The authorized operations: prediction_braking and local_comparison. local_comparison requires the exact adopted parameter/value, but `adopted_parameter` is null in role_context. So local_comparison is not available (no adopted parameter). So use prediction_braking.

prediction_braking: "At one saved projected state, compare recorded input with instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed short horizon. Can measure local endpoint speed/position differences. Cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same result; cannot identify the dominant settling cause."

Requires update_id >= 1. Choose a late-window update in the settling window. The late window is ~0.30-0.35 s. Update 30 has measured_speed 1.329 (endpoint 0.31 s), update 29 at t=0.29 has speed 0.8619. Update 30 controller start time 0.30, effective_horizon... let's check: fact_catalog shows updates[3].effective_horizon update_id 22 = 10, updates[7].effective_horizon update_id 34 = 1. Hmm, the effective horizon for update 34 is 1. For update 30, I don't have direct data. Actually I recall the "updates" array indices are per-page slices, so update_id field tells the actual id.

I should possibly read evidence to choose. But I have a limited read budget: "At most two successful reading turns, then select the check." Phase tools include evidence.read and diagnosis.inspect_evidence. But budget-wise I could just do the check directly. Evidence turn limit: 2; successful_read_turns 0; turns_used 0. Also "Model calls" budget: 6 per phase, 24 project; remaining model_calls 19.

I think one call is fine — choose update_id directly. But do I want to verify effective horizon? prediction_braking doesn't require a saved effective horizon matching (only local_comparison does per the instructions: "local_comparison ... requires the exact adopted parameter/value and a saved effective plan horizon of 0.01 s"). Since adopted_parameter is null, local_comparison is out.

So: prediction_braking at update_id = 30 (late window, highest measured speed, actual input available via measured_initial_state and actual_tension_n for that update).

Hmm — check the inventory: applied_tensions has 35 records covering updates 0..34, so update 30 has an actual_tension_n. Good. The host binds the update's exact measured_initial_state and the operation-defined input.

Which update best discriminates? Hypotheses:
- H1: The recorded late-window plan applies near-zero braking authority (tip speed persists because commanded input leaves the tip moving at high speed at the horizon endpoint).
- H2: An instantaneous braking box solution would substantially reduce endpoint tip speed over the 10 ms horizon, i.e., the applied input is not braking-limited locally.
- Also the model mismatch hypothesis: if the braking box predicts essentially the same endpoint as the recorded input, the check can't separate.

Discriminating observation: difference between recorded-input predicted endpoint tip speed and braking-box endpoint tip speed at 10 ms; difference in endpoint position.

Acceptance criteria: the check returns both endpoints (recorded and braking) for the chosen update at the fixed horizon; if the difference in endpoint speed is within the numerical tolerance of zero, the check does not discriminate H1 vs H2.

Work limits: wall_s <= 300; prediction_evaluations=2.

Also I need fixed_conditions: model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit_euler, 0.002 s step, 0.01 s horizon, saved projected state at update 30, world frame for tip vectors.

Metrics: endpoint tip speed (m/s), endpoint tip position difference (m).

unresolved: seed/shallow-iterate vs weighting vs horizon vs backend-model mismatch; cannot identify dominant settling cause; a 10 ms probe cannot explain the entire settling failure.

Let me pick the update. Which one? The late window is where settling fails: 0.30-0.35 s. Update 30 (start 0.30 s) has the largest measured speed (1.329 m/s at endpoint 0.31). Update 34 effective_horizon=1 (degenerate). Hmm — an update with effective_horizon 1 is near the end. Choose update 30 or 33/34.

I'd choose update_id 30: the largest sampled measured tip speed in the late settling window, controller start 0.30 s, endpoint 0.31 s, actual tension available. Actually wait — is update 30's actual_tension_n displayed? fact catalog has "detail.evidence.observations.updates[3].actual_input_n ... update_id 11, 19, 22". Not exhaustive but the inventory says all 35 retained. prediction_braking uses current actual_tension_n for the host binding — fine.

Actually, maybe better to choose the update whose measured speed is largest in the window = 1.329 at update 30. Yes.

local_question: "At saved projected state of controller update 30 (late settling window), does an instantaneous braking-box input reduce the fixed 10 ms horizon endpoint tip speed relative to the recorded applied tension, and by how much in speed and position?"

Hypotheses (min 2):
H1: With recorded applied tensions held over the 0.01 s horizon, the projected tip speed remains well above the 0.02 m/s settling scale (no local braking).
H2: An instantaneous braking-box solution at the same saved state yields a materially lower endpoint tip speed than the recorded input, indicating locally available braking authority that the recorded plan does not use.
H3? maybe include the non-separable hypothesis: H1 and H2 predict indistinguishable endpoints (model mismatch dominates).

discriminating_observations: list the endpoint tip speeds and position difference.

Acceptance criteria: the probe returns both endpoint speed values (recorded vs braking) and the endpoint position difference; if |Δspeed| is within numerical resolution, the check does not separate H1 from H2.

Let me write the call. Fields required: hypotheses, fixed_conditions, metrics, work_limits, acceptance_criteria, local_question, discriminating_observations, unresolved, operation, update_id.

Note: do NOT supply fact_selectors, evidence observed etc. Also "Do not supply ... report source/gates or recommendation configuration_scope". There's a "prior_result" field — optional; skip or provide prior report ref? It says prior_result anyOf EvidenceRef. Probably optional. I'll omit.

additional_need, changed_factor, changed_parameter, changed_value: omit (prediction_braking requires no adoption).

Should I do a read first? The instruction says I may make up to three independent evidence reads. It may be safer to verify update 30's actual tension and effective horizon before choosing. But cost: model calls. Phase remaining model calls 6. Actually the safest is to just pick update 30, since the host binds state and input. Hmm, but is prediction_braking valid if update 30's effective horizon isn't saved? For prediction_braking, the horizon is host-fixed at 0.01 s. Fine.

One consideration: "prediction_braking uses current actual_tension_n". Fine.

Let me also consider whether update 34 (effective_horizon=1) is a better "braking" candidate — no, its horizon is 1 control interval but the host horizon is fixed at 0.01 s regardless.

I'll go with update_id 30.

Let me write out nicely.

Also note "unresolved": must include hypotheses this probe cannot separate, and limits independent of outcome. Include: seed/shallow-iterate vs objective weighting vs horizon effects vs backend-model mismatch (these predict same endpoint difference); the 10 ms local probe cannot explain the full settling failure or identify dominant cause; tension/force-limit saturation sub-question needs per-update force_limit_saturated and tension_tracking_error_n not read.

Write the tool call.
